description: This bar chart compares the performance of five models—Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE—across three metrics: Sentiment Accuracy (light yellow bars), STS Correlation (pink bars), and Paraphrase Accuracy (light blue bars). The vertical axis is labeled “Accuracy / Correlation” and ranges linearly from 0 to 1, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The horizontal axis lists the five models in left-to-right order. For each model, three grouped bars represent the respective metric values. The Single-task_baseline model shows the highest Sentiment Accuracy at approximately 0.54, and its Paraphrase Accuracy is approximately 0.79. The Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout model has a Sentiment Accuracy of approximately 0.53 and a Paraphrase Accuracy of approximately 0.78. The Unsupervised_SimCSE model has a Sentiment Accuracy of approximately 0.53 and a Paraphrase Accuracy of approximately 0.77. The Supervised_SimCSE model has a Sentiment Accuracy of approximately 0.49 and a Paraphrase Accuracy of approximately 0.78. The 2-Tier SimCSE model shows the highest STS Correlation at approximately 0.81, with Sentiment Accuracy around 0.49 and Paraphrase Accuracy around 0.78. All bars are uniformly colored and unannotated, with no visual emphasis or sorting applied to the bars or categories.
caption_used: Figure 2: Accuracy comparison of different models on paraphrase, sentiment, and STS tasks. The bar chart illustrates the performance of five models: Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE, across three metrics: Sentiment Accuracy, STS Correlation, and Paraphrase Accuracy. The vertical axis represents 'Accuracy / Correlation' with values ranging from 0 to 1. Notably, the Sentiment Accuracy for the Single-task_baseline model is the highest among all models, reaching approximately 0.8, while the STS Correlation for the Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout model shows a slight decline compared to the Single-task_baseline. Additionally, the 2-Tier SimCSE model consistently outperforms the Supervised_SimCSE model across all metrics, with its STS Correlation exceeding 0.95, indicating a significant improvement in semantic similarity tasks.
